What the dashboard measures

How the client could use it

Explore interest beyond the post



The sample CSV treats reach as the sum of post reach. A person may appear in the reach of more than one post, so this is not unique campaign reach. Profile actions are a total action count, not a count of unique people or reservations.

title: Instagram Content & Engagement
section: From a prototype to client reporting
text:
From a prototype to client reporting
I would replace the sample CSV with an approved Instagram Insights export, use the same reporting period for each comparison, and document how each metric is defined. I would also code message styles and compare similar posting conditions. If tagged link data becomes available, I could examine Instagram referral activity separately.
For the pilot, I would compare a baseline period with a planned content test. Higher engagement alone would not establish that Instagram increased reservations. A small sample, repeat exposure, different posting times, and other marketing activity could affect the results.

title: Instagram Content & Engagement
text:
How this was built
The dashboard uses Quarto’s format: dashboard, cards, a chart, and a table. Its values were calculated from the included CSV during project preparation. The chart and table are static; after replacing the data, their summaries must be recalculated and the site rendered again. This version does not connect to Instagram or update automatically.

title: Find work by topic
text:
What is a listing?
A Quarto listing builds an organized collection of pages using their metadata. Instead of adding every project link manually, I can place a QMD file in projects/ and give it a title, description, and categories. The listing updates when I render the website.

title: Find work by topic
text:
How I set it up
listing:
  id: portfolio
  contents: projects
  type: grid
  fields: [title, description, categories]
  categories: true
  filter-ui: true
  sort: title
A project page supplies the information used on its card:
title: "Instagram dashboard prototype"
description: "A demonstration of content performance reporting."
categories: [Analytics, CEP]

text:
How this helps my portfolio
I could organize future work into analytics, content, and research categories. A hiring manager could quickly find a dashboard or read about a project’s purpose and limitations. I would add real results only after checking the data and confirming permission to share it.

text:
Connecting the files
My _quarto.yml loads the base theme, my SCSS theme, and the CSS file:
format:
  html:
    theme: [cosmo, theme.scss]
    css: styles.css
The same file defines the four navigation tabs. This avoids rebuilding the navigation on every page.

title: Making a Quarto website easier to read
text:
Keeping the site usable
I included visible keyboard focus outlines, descriptive links, and a mobile media query that reduces the hero padding and photo area on small screens. Meaningful images need alternative text. I also kept the main information in text so color alone does not communicate meaning.
Quarto HTML theming guide
